
```{r setup-options}
# packages and options
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
})
options(knitr.kable.NA = "", scipen = 100)
```

This supplement accompanies the paper. S1 and S2 give the full results of the simulation and
the plasmode study, S3 the comparators, S4 the approaches that did not work, S5 misspecified truths
and basis size, S6 data and code. The CL2 algebra, the descriptions of both studies' set-ups and the
computing times are in Appendices A--C of the paper. Every number is computed from the study's
summary files when the document is rendered.

Coverage, its 5% quantile over the grid (lower tail), relative error, relative half-width, detection
rate and interval score are defined in Section 2.4 of the paper. In addition, a *setting* is one
combination of design factors of the simulation, with 200 replicate data sets, and the *wrong-sign
rate* is the share of all grid points at which an interval excludes zero on the wrong side. Monte
Carlo (MC) standard errors are computed over replicates; for a grid-averaged coverage, from the
replicate-level grid averages, so the correlation of coverage indicators across grid points is
accounted for. REML + CL2 and NCV + CL2 denote the REML or curve-blocked NCV fit with the CL2
covariance of Appendix A of the paper and normal critical values; model-based intervals use mgcv's
$\mathbf V_c$ for REML fits and $\mathbf V_p$ for NCV fits, because in the mgcv build of the study
$\mathbf V_c$ of an NCV fit holds only the smoothing-parameter correction and is not a valid
covariance (S6). Error processes of the main factorial: independent, rough stationary (an
exponential correlation with a nugget) and smooth (from DTI residual curves). Signal levels:
low, default and high ($R^2 = 0.2, 0.5, 0.8$ for Gaussian responses; $\sqrt S = 0.5$ (default) and 1 on
the link scale for Poisson and binary responses, where "low" and "default" coincide). Bases: the
default, and bases with 2× and 4× finer knots. Functional covariate: rich (the default spectrum)
or low-rank. The plasmode truths are the fitted means of the REML fit (*REML-fitted truth*), of the
NCV fit (*NCV-fitted truth*), and of a refit with every smoothing parameter at the geometric mean of
the REML and NCV values (*midpoint truth*).

# S1 Simulation study {#sec-s2}

The design is described in Appendix B.1 of the paper.

## S1.1 Coverage per setting

```{r t-s2-cov-1}
#| output: asis
t1 <- supp_cov_wide |> select(-cell)
t1_short <- c("NCV + CL2, widened by NCV–REML difference" = "NCV wid.", "NCV + CL2 (freq.), widened by NCV–REML difference" = "NCV wid. (freq.)",
  "NCV, model-based" = "NCV model", "REML, model-based" = "REML model", "AR(1) working model" = "AR(1)", "NCV + CL2" = "NCV+CL2", "REML + CL2" = "REML+CL2")
names(t1) <- ifelse(names(t1) %in% names(t1_short), t1_short[names(t1)], names(t1))
stab(t1, "Grid-averaged coverage (MC SE) of the mean and $\\beta(s,t)$ per setting and interval. REML model / NCV model: model-based intervals of the REML / NCV fit; NCV wid.: NCV + CL2 widened in quadrature by the NCV–REML difference (S4.1(b)), with the Bayesian or the frequentist (freq.) CL2; AR(1): AR(1) working model.", long = TRUE, font = 5, landscape = TRUE)
```

```{r t-s2-ag-1}
#| output: asis
ag_arms <- c("REML, model-based" = "REML model", "REML + CL2" = "REML+CL2", "NCV + CL2" = "NCV+CL2",
  "NCV + CL2, widened by NCV–REML difference" = "NCV wid.")
ag_est <- c("α(t)", "γ(t)")
ag_w <- supp_ag_wide |>
  mutate(estimand = if_else(estimand == "f(x,t)", "α(t)", estimand)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = estimand, values_from = all_of(names(ag_arms)), names_glue = "{estimand}|{.value}")
ag_cols <- paste0(rep(ag_est, each = length(ag_arms)), "|", names(ag_arms))
ag_w <- relabel(ag_w[, c(setdiff(names(ag_w), ag_cols), ag_cols)])
ag_id <- ncol(ag_w) - length(ag_cols)
k <- knitr::kable(ag_w, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, longtable = TRUE, linesep = "",
  col.names = c(names(ag_w)[seq_len(ag_id)], rep(unname(ag_arms), 2)),
  caption = "Coverage (MC SE) of $\\alpha(t)$ and $\\gamma(t)$ per setting; for the smooth-effect settings the first group of columns holds $f(x,t)$. Interval labels as in the previous table.")
kableExtra::kable_styling(k, font_size = 5, latex_options = "repeat_header") |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(setNames(ag_id, " "), "α(t) or f(x,t)" = length(ag_arms), "γ(t)" = length(ag_arms))) |>
  kableExtra::landscape()
```

## S1.2 Lower tails, number of curves, signal and truth roughness

```{r s2-3}
tq_dep <- \(a, e, g) tail_tab$q05_min[tail_tab$arm == ARM_LABELS[a] & tail_tab$estimand %in% ESTIMAND_LABELS[e] & tail_tab$G == g & tail_tab$dependence == "dependent"]
stc <- \(a, tr, err = "fpc") st$coverage_mean[st$arm == a & st$truth == tr & st$error == err]
```

In the dependent main-factorial settings, the worst setting's 5% quantile of pointwise coverage for
the mean and $\beta$ is `r rng(tq_dep("reml_cl2", c("mean", "beta"), 100))` for REML + CL2 at
$G = 100$ and `r rng(tq_dep("reml_cl2", c("mean", "beta"), 40))` at $G = 40$; for model-based intervals
it is as low as `r rng(tq_dep("reml_model", c("mean", "beta"), 100))`. With 40 instead of 100 curves
REML + CL2 loses `r rng_pp(gl("reml_cl2"))` of coverage (means per family and estimand; coverage by
$G$ in the first table under *Twenty curves*), NCV + CL2
`r rng_pp(gl("ncv_cl2"))`. Signal strength changes little. Truth roughness matters for NCV + CL2:
with the rough truth and smooth errors it covers $\beta$ at `r rng(stc("ncv_cl2", "wiggly"))`
(smooth truth `r rng(stc("ncv_cl2", "smooth"))`), REML + CL2 at `r rng(stc("reml_cl2", "wiggly"))`.

```{r t-s2-tail-1}
#| output: asis
stab(tail_tab, "5% quantile of pointwise coverage (minimum and median over main-factorial settings) and minimum grid-averaged coverage, by dependence, $G$, estimand and interval.", font = 7)
```

*Twenty curves.* The main factorial was also run with $G = 20$, the first 20 curves of each
replicate, so the three numbers of curves share their draws (first table below; means over each
family's settings for coverage, medians for relative error and detection). Under dependent errors
REML + CL2 covers the mean, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ at `r rng(lcv("reml_cl2", 20))` with 20 curves,
`r rng(lcv("reml_cl2", 40))` with 40 and `r rng(lcv("reml_cl2", 100))` with 100, and $\alpha(t)$ at
`r rng(lcv("reml_cl2", 20, e = "alpha"))` with 20. NCV + CL2 falls to
`r rng(lcv("ncv_cl2", 20, e = c("mean", "beta", "alpha", "gamma")))` with 20 curves, the model-based REML intervals to
`r rng(lcv("reml_model", 20, e = c("mean", "beta", "alpha", "gamma")))`. Under independent errors every interval undercovers
binary $\alpha(t)$ and $\gamma(t)$ with 20 curves, the model-based one included
(`r rng(lcv("reml_model", 20, "independent", c("alpha", "gamma"), "binomial"))`). REML's median relative
error for $\beta$ under dependence is `r rng(lcv("reml_cl2", 20, e = "beta", col = "rel"), 2)` with 20
curves, NCV's `r rng(lcv("ncv_cl2", 20, e = "beta", col = "rel"), 2)`; REML + CL2 detects
`r rng(lcv("reml_cl2", 20, e = "beta", col = "det"), 2)` of the clearly non-zero grid points of $\beta$,
NCV + CL2 `r rng(lcv("ncv_cl2", 20, e = "beta", col = "det"), 2)`. With the Satterthwaite critical
value (second table; default signal, as for 40 and 100 curves), REML + CL2 covers the mean, $\beta$
and $\gamma$ at `r rng(lsv("satt", 20))` under dependence with 20 curves, against `r rng(lsv("z", 20))`
with $z$ and `r rng(lsv("t", 20))` with $t_{G-1}$, at `r rng(lsv("satt", 20, col = "wr"), 2)` times the
width of the $z$ interval. Binary $\alpha(t)$ stays at
`r f(lsv("satt", 20, e = "alpha", fam = "binomial"), 3)` under dependence and
`r f(lsv("satt", 20, "independent", e = "alpha", fam = "binomial"), 3)` under independent errors, and
under independent Gaussian and Poisson errors the intervals overcover
(`r rng(lsv("satt", 20, "independent", fam = c("gaussian", "poisson")))`).

## S1.3 Error structures and extended families

```{r s2-4}
gd2 <- \(v, err = c("ou", "fpc")) dense$estimate[dense$value == v & dense$error %in% err]
```

From $D = 61$ to $D = 241$ grid points per curve, the coverage of $\beta$ by model-based intervals drops
by `r rng_pp(-gd2("coverage_reml_model"))` under dependent errors, while REML + CL2 changes by
`r rng_pp(gd2("coverage_reml_cl2"))`. A variance profile along $t$ changes no interval. Variance that
depends on the scalar covariate breaks the model-based intervals for $\gamma(t)$
(`r rng(hv("reml_model", "gamma", c("fpc_het", "fpc_raw_het")))`), not REML + CL2
(`r rng(hv("reml_cl2", "gamma", c("fpc_het", "fpc_raw_het")))`). Under misregistration REML + CL2
covers the Gaussian estimands at `r rng(wv("reml_cl2", "gaussian"))`; for misregistered Poisson
responses every interval undercovers the mean (REML + CL2 `r rng(wv("reml_cl2", "poisson"))`).
Sign-changing correlation: model-based `r rng(c(osc_tab$reml_model))`, REML + CL2
`r rng(c(osc_tab$reml_cl2))`. Extended families under smooth errors: model-based
`r rng(fv("reml_model"))`, REML + CL2 `r rng(fv("reml_cl2"))`.

## S1.4 Studentized errors

```{r s1-4-bin}
zb_a <- ZS |> filter(fit == "REML", block == "core", family == "binomial", estimand == "alpha", basis == "default")
zba <- \(dep, g, col) mean(zb_a[[col]][(zb_a$error != "iid") == dep & zb_a$G == g])
zbs <- \(sig, col = "z_sd_cl2") zb_a[[col]][zb_a$error == "iid" & zb_a$G == 40 & zb_a$signal == sig]
abl_bin <- readr::read_csv("ablation/summaries/ablation-cells.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(family == "binomial", crit == "z", G == 40, arm %in% c("cl2e_b", "fix_cl2e_b"), estimand %in% c("alpha", "gamma"))
abv <- \(err, e, a) abl_bin$coverage[abl_bin$error == err & abl_bin$estimand == e & abl_bin$arm == a]
```

The studentized error $z = (\text{estimate} - \text{truth})/\mathrm{SE}$ of the REML fit, pooled over grid
points and replicates, is descriptive: an SD above one with mean near zero indicates standard errors
that are too small; a shifted mean indicates bias. Pooling cannot separate a global scale error from
local biases of opposite sign. In the dependent main-factorial settings at $G = 100$ the SD of $z$ with
the CL2 standard error is `r rng(zcv("z_sd_cl2"))` for $\beta$ (model-based standard error:
`r rng(zcv("z_sd_model"))`). The intercept $\alpha(t)$ of binary responses behaves differently.
Under independent errors at $G = 40$ its studentized CL2 error has mean
`r f(zba(FALSE, 40, "z_mean_cl2"), 3)` and SD `r f(zba(FALSE, 40, "z_sd_cl2"), 2)` (model-based standard
error: mean `r f(zba(FALSE, 40, "z_mean_model"), 3)`, SD `r f(zba(FALSE, 40, "z_sd_model"), 2)`). These are
averages over the two signal levels: the SD is `r f(zbs("mid"), 2)` at the default signal and
`r f(zbs("high"), 2)` at the high signal. These values are compatible with a CL2 standard error that
is too small for this term, but they do not exclude local bias. Under dependence the studentized error is in
addition shifted (mean `r zbe_rng(40)` at $G = 40$ and `r zbe_rng(100)` at $G = 100$, per dependent error
process, averaged over the signal levels; SD `r f(zba(TRUE, 100, "z_sd_cl2"), 2)` at $G = 100$).
The covariance-components runs (Appendix A.6 of the paper) add a diagnostic. Fixing the smoothing
parameters at their typical value raises binary $\gamma(t)$ under independent errors at $G = 40$ from
`r f(abv("iid", "gamma", "cl2e_b"), 3)` to `r f(abv("iid", "gamma", "fix_cl2e_b"), 3)`, and binary
$\alpha(t)$ under smooth errors from `r f(abv("fpc", "alpha", "cl2e_b"), 3)` to
`r f(abv("fpc", "alpha", "fix_cl2e_b"), 3)`; binary $\alpha(t)$ under independent errors stays at
`r f(abv("iid", "alpha", "fix_cl2e_b"), 3)` (`r f(abv("iid", "alpha", "cl2e_b"), 3)` with selected
smoothing parameters). For $\gamma(t)$, and for $\alpha(t)$ under dependence, a large part of the
shortfall therefore looks like variability of the selected smoothing parameters, which CL2 ignores;
for $\alpha(t)$ under independent errors it remains unexplained. Satterthwaite degrees of freedom
widen these intervals only slightly (Appendix A.7 of the paper), so they cannot compensate a standard
error that is too small by about a fifth.

```{r t-s2-z-1}
#| output: asis
zs_vals <- c("z_mean_cl2", "z_sd_cl2", "share_big_cl2", "z_mean_model", "z_sd_model", "share_big_model")
zs_est <- c("mean", "beta", "alpha", "gamma")
zs_w <- zs_tab |>
  mutate(estimand = if_else(estimand == "f", "beta", estimand)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = estimand, values_from = all_of(zs_vals), names_glue = "{estimand}|{.value}")
zs_cols <- paste0(rep(zs_est, each = length(zs_vals)), "|", zs_vals)
zs_w <- relabel(zs_w[, c(setdiff(names(zs_w), zs_cols), zs_cols)])
zs_id <- ncol(zs_w) - length(zs_cols)
k <- knitr::kable(zs_w, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, longtable = TRUE, digits = 3, linesep = "",
  col.names = c(names(zs_w)[seq_len(zs_id)], rep(c("mean", "SD", "|z|>1.96"), 8)),
  caption = "Pooled studentized errors of the REML fit with the CL2 and the model-based standard error: mean, SD and share of $|z| > 1.96$ (means over settings), per estimand; the $\\beta(s,t)$ columns hold $f(x,t)$ in the smooth-effect settings. Mean only for Gaussian responses.")
k <- kableExtra::kable_styling(k, font_size = 5, latex_options = "repeat_header") |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(setNames(zs_id, " "), rep(c("CL2" = 3, "model" = 3), 4))) |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(setNames(zs_id, " "), "E(Y | X)" = 6, "β(s,t) or f(x,t)" = 6, "α(t)" = 6, "γ(t)" = 6)) |>
  kableExtra::landscape()
cat("\\begingroup\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{2.5pt}\n", k, "\n\\endgroup\n", sep = "")
```

## S1.5 Estimation

```{r s2-6}
bshare2 <- \(fit_sel, tr, e = "beta", err = c("ou", "fpc")) bv_tab$bias_share[bv_tab$fit == fit_sel & bv_tab$truth == tr & bv_tab$estimand == e & bv_tab$error %in% err & bv_tab$G == 100]
```

Under dependent errors the NCV/REML MSE ratio for $\beta$, geometric mean over the main-factorial
settings of each error process, is `r rng(pe("beta", c("ou", "fpc")))` (independent errors:
`r rng(pe("beta", "iid"))`); for the mean `r rng(pe("mean", c("ou", "fpc")))` (same summary; per
setting at $G = 100$ the mean's ratio is
`r rng(MSE_RATIO$ratio[MSE_RATIO$block == "core" & MSE_RATIO$G == 100 & MSE_RATIO$error != "iid" & MSE_RATIO$estimand == "mean"])`). NCV's advantage for
$\beta$ does not vanish under independent errors: for Gaussian responses the per-setting ratio is
`r rng(MSE_RATIO$ratio[MSE_RATIO$block == "core" & MSE_RATIO$error == "iid" & MSE_RATIO$family == "gaussian" & MSE_RATIO$estimand == "beta"])`
there. Part of the gap therefore reflects the smooth truths, which favour more smoothing, and not
only the dependence. With the rough truth the
$\beta$ ratio is `r rng(rough$ratio[rough$estimand == "beta"])`. REML's excess error is variance: the
squared-bias share of REML's $\beta$ error in the dependent settings at $G = 100$ is
`r rng(bshare2("REML", "smooth"))`, of NCV's `r rng(bshare2("NCV", "smooth"))`; with the rough truth
NCV's share rises to `r rng(bshare2("NCV", "wiggly", err = "fpc"))`. REML's surface EDF exceeds NCV's
by a factor `r rng(er("beta(s,t)", c("ou", "fpc")))` under dependence
(`r rng(er("beta(s,t)", "iid"))` under independence). Pointwise NCV, which leaves out single grid
points, is no substitute for curve blocks: its $\beta$ MSE is `r rng(pwv("beta", c("fpc", "osc")))`
times REML's under smooth and sign-changing errors. A low-rank covariate gives a $\beta$ ratio of
`r rng(lowr$ratio[lowr$estimand == "beta" & lowr$error == "fpc"])` under smooth errors.

```{r t-s2-mse-6}

mse_w <- supp_mse_wide |>
  mutate(estimand = if_else(estimand == "f(x,t)", "β(s,t)", estimand)) |>
  rename(REML = `MSE REML`, NCV = `MSE NCV`, ratio = `ratio NCV/REML`) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = estimand, values_from = c(REML, NCV, ratio), names_glue = "{estimand}|{.value}")
mse_cols <- paste0(rep(mse_est, each = 3), "|", c("REML", "NCV", "ratio"))

k <- knitr::kable(mse_w, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, longtable = TRUE, digits = 4, linesep = "",
  col.names = c(names(mse_w)[seq_len(n_id)], rep(c("REML", "NCV", "ratio"), 4)),
  caption = "Integrated MSE of the REML and NCV fits per setting and estimand, and their paired ratio NCV/REML (95\\% bootstrap interval); for the smooth-effect settings the $\\beta(s,t)$ columns hold $f(x,t)$.")

  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(setNames(n_id, " "), setNames(rep(3, 4), mse_est))) |>
  kableExtra::landscape()
```

## S1.6 Relative error, half-width and detection per setting

Under dependent errors the median relative error of $\beta$ over settings is
`r f(rs("beta", "dependent", "reml_cl2", "rel_error"), 2)` for REML and
`r f(rs("beta", "dependent", "ncv_cl2", "rel_error"), 2)` for NCV; under independent errors
`r f(rs("beta", "independent", "reml_cl2", "rel_error"), 2)` and
`r f(rs("beta", "independent", "ncv_cl2", "rel_error"), 2)`. In the main factorial the REML/NCV ratio
of relative errors is `r rng(rr("dep"), 1)` under dependent and `r rng(rr("iid"), 1)` under independent
errors. Wrong-sign exclusions of the CL2 intervals stay rare (at most
`r f(rs("beta", "dependent", "reml_cl2", "wrong_sign_max"), 3)` of the grid for REML + CL2 and
`r f(rs("beta", "dependent", "ncv_cl2", "wrong_sign_max"), 3)` for NCV + CL2); model-based REML
intervals reach `r f(rs("beta", "dependent", "reml_model", "wrong_sign_max"), 2)`.

## S1.7 Satterthwaite critical values beyond the main factorial

```{r s1-7}
satx_n <- n_distinct(SATX$cell)
satx_lowb <- unique(satx_low_tab$block[satx_low_tab$block != "misregistration"])
satx_cov <- \(g) mean(satx_con$diff[satx_con$G == g])
satx_wr <- \(g) mean(satx_con$width_ratio[satx_con$G == g])
```

REML + CL2 intervals with the per-point Satterthwaite critical value of Appendix A.7 of the paper were
computed from the stored REML fits for every synthetic setting outside the main factorial
(`r satx_n` settings, including those with 20 curves and the zero surface) and for the plasmode
combinations with curve flips (S2.1). Paired with the normal critical value on the same replicates, the
Satterthwaite interval never covered less: the smallest difference over all settings, plasmode
combinations and estimands is `r pp(satt_min_gain, 2)`. Over the extension settings it adds
`r pp(satx_cov(40))` of coverage with 40 curves and `r pp(satx_cov(100))` with 100 on average, at
`r f(satx_wr(40), 2)` and `r f(satx_wr(100), 2)` times the width (first table). Coverage stays below
`r f(LEVEL - ADEQUATE, 2)` in `r nrow(satx_low_tab)` combinations of setting and estimand (second
table): misregistered count and binary responses, and the binary intercept or scalar effect in the
`r paste(satx_lowb, collapse = ", ")` settings. The per-point degrees of freedom (third table) are
about a third of $G - 1$ for the mean, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ in every synthetic setting and larger for
$\alpha(t)$; on the plasmode data they spread more.

```{r t-s1-satt-ext}
  "REML + CL2 with the normal ($z$) and the Satterthwaite (Satt.) critical value in the extension settings: grid-averaged coverage per block, number of curves and estimand (mean over the block's settings; $\\beta$ includes $f(x,t)$ of the smooth-effect settings; misregistered count and binary settings score the mean only), and the mean width ratio.", font = 6)
```

## S1.8 A zero coefficient surface

```{r s1-8}
nul_diff <- with(null_other, reml_cl2[!is.na(core)] - core[!is.na(core)])
```

The zero-surface settings set $\beta \equiv 0$ in the smooth-truth setting at the default signal
(Appendix B.1 of the paper). The share of grid points at which a pointwise 95% interval excludes zero
estimates the pointwise false-positive rate, nominally 0.05 (first table). Under smooth errors
REML + CL2 has `r rng(nsv("reml_cl2"), 3)` with $z$, `r rng(nsv("reml_cl2_t"), 3)` with $t_{G-1}$ and
`r rng(nsv("reml_cl2_satt"), 3)` with the Satterthwaite critical value. The model-based intervals have
`r rng(nsv("reml_model"), 2)` (REML) and `r rng(nsv("ncv_model"), 2)` (NCV), NCV + CL2
`r rng(nsv("ncv_cl2"), 2)`. NCV + CL2 widened by the NCV--REML difference has the lowest rate under
smooth errors (`r rng(nsv("ncv_cl2_bias"), 3)`), but not because it is calibrated: its variance adds the
squared difference between the NCV and the REML estimate, and under a zero surface the REML estimate is
far from zero (second table), so its intervals are wide. Under independent errors the Gaussian setting
with 40 curves stands out: REML + CL2 has `r f(nsv("reml_cl2", "iid", "gaussian", 40), 3)`
(MC SE `r f(nsv("reml_cl2", "iid", "gaussian", 40, "fpr_se"), 3)`), with the Satterthwaite critical
value `r f(nsv("reml_cl2_satt", "iid", "gaussian", 40), 3)`, against
`r f(nsv("reml_cl2", "iid", "gaussian", 100), 3)` with 100 curves. Its excluded points concentrate in a
minority of replicates (`r f(nsv("reml_cl2", "iid", "gaussian", 40, "share_gt_5pct"), 2)` have more than
5% of the grid excluding zero; the 90% quantile of the per-replicate rate is
`r f(nsv("reml_cl2", "iid", "gaussian", 40, "fpr_q90"), 2)`). In most replicates REML shrinks the
surface towards the null space of its penalty; intervals for terms shrunk this far are known to behave
poorly [@MarraWood2012].

The second table is descriptive. The share of replicates with at least one grid point, or with more than
5% of the grid, excluding zero is not an error rate of pointwise intervals; whether $\beta$ is zero
everywhere needs a simultaneous band or a global test, which the study does not evaluate. Under smooth
errors REML's estimate of the zero surface has a root-mean-square size of
`r rng(nsv("reml_cl2", col = "rms_rel"), 2)` times that of the non-zero surface of the corresponding
main-factorial setting, NCV's `r rng(nsv("ncv_cl2", col = "rms_rel"), 2)` times; under independent errors
both are small (`r rng(c(nsv("reml_cl2", "iid", col = "rms_rel"), nsv("ncv_cl2", "iid", col = "rms_rel")), 2)`).
The zero surface hardly changes the other estimands (third table): REML + CL2 coverage of
$\alpha(t)$ and $\gamma(t)$ differs from that in the matching non-zero setting by `r rng_pp(nul_diff)`.

```{r t-s1-null-fpr}
#| output: asis
stab(null_fpr_tab, "Zero surface: pointwise false-positive rate (MC SE), the share of grid points at which the 95% interval excludes zero, mean over replicates; nominal 0.05. NCV+CL2 widened: NCV + CL2 with the squared NCV–REML difference added to the variance.", font = 6)
```

```{r t-s1-null-desc}
#| output: asis
stab(null_desc_tab, "Zero surface, descriptive: share of replicates with at least one grid point / with more than 5% of the grid excluding zero, per interval (not error rates of pointwise intervals); root-mean-square size of the REML and NCV estimates over the grid (mean over replicates), absolute and relative to the non-zero surface of the corresponding main-factorial setting.", font = 6)
```

```{r t-s1-null-other}

stab(null_other_tab, "Zero surface: coverage of the mean, $\\alpha(t)$ and $\\gamma(t)$ per interval, and of REML + CL2 in the matching non-zero setting (same $\\alpha$ and $\\gamma$; the mean differs).", font = 6)
```

## S1.9 A principal component term for a low-rank covariate {#sec-s1-ffpc}

```{r s1-9}
ff_rich <- \(rule, arm = "ffpc_cl2", col = "rel_rmse") ffv(FFPC_RICH, rule, arm, col)
ff_smooth_rich <- setdiff(FFPC_RICH, FFPC_DESIGN$cell[FFPC_DESIGN$truth != "smooth"])
ff_rough <- FFPC_DESIGN$cell[FFPC_DESIGN$truth != "smooth"]
# K = 5: error between those of ff NCV and ff REML in every rich-covariate setting
stopifnot(
  all(ff_rich("k5") > ff_rich("k3", "ff_ncv_cl2")),
  all(ff_rich("k5") < ff_rich("k3", "ff_reml_cl2")),
  length(ff_rough) == 1
)
ffp99 <- FFPC_PILOT |> filter(pve == "p099")
ffp99_v <- \(arm, col = "rel_rmse") ffp99[[col]][ffp99$arm == arm]
# range of median numbers of components (may be half-integers)
kr <- \(x) {
  x <- sort(unique(x))
  if (length(x) == 1) format(x) else paste0(format(min(x)), "–", format(max(x)))
}
```

In the eight settings of the next table (all with smooth errors and REML fits), the functional term
was also fitted with refund's `ffpc()` term, on the same simulated data as the `ff()` fits. `ffpc()`
estimates the leading functional principal components of the covariate curves and regresses the
response on their scores, with one coefficient function $b_k(t)$ per component in the basis and
penalty used for $\alpha(t)$. The surface estimate is
$\hat\beta(s,t) = \sum_{k=1}^K \psi_k(s)\,\hat b_k(t)$, where the $\psi_k$ are the estimated
eigenfunctions scaled so that the integrals of the centred covariate curves against them reproduce
the scores. Its standard errors use the CL2 covariance of the $b_k$ (full block, with
$\mathbf V_p - \mathbf V_e$) and are conditional on the estimated eigenfunctions; the intervals use
the normal critical value. The number of components $K$ is fixed at 3 or 5, or is the smallest number
that explains 95% or 90% of the covariate's variance. Accuracy is measured by the relative
root-mean-square error
$\{\sum_{r,j}(\hat\beta_{rj} - \beta_j)^2/\sum_{r,j}\beta_j^2\}^{1/2}$, pooled over replicates $r$
and grid points $j$ (not the median over replicates of Section 2.4 of the paper); the `ff()` columns
are the study's REML + CL2 and NCV + CL2 on the same replicates, with the same measures.

With the low-rank covariate, the components that explain 95% of its variance (median
$K = `r ffv(FFPC_LR, "p095", col = "K_median")`$) estimate $\beta$ with relative RMSE
`r f(ffv(FFPC_LR, "p095"), 2)`, against `r f(ffv(FFPC_LR, "k3", "ff_reml_cl2"), 2)` for `ff()` with
REML and `r f(ffv(FFPC_LR, "k3", "ff_ncv_cl2"), 2)` with NCV. Their CL2 intervals cover
`r f(ffv(FFPC_LR, "p095", col = "coverage"), 3)` (MC SE
`r f(ffv(FFPC_LR, "p095", col = "coverage_mcse"), 3)`) at
`r f(ffv(FFPC_LR, "p095", col = "hw_vs_reml"), 2)` times the half-width of `ff()` REML + CL2; with
five components they cover `r f(ffv(FFPC_LR, "k5", col = "coverage"), 3)` at relative RMSE
`r f(ffv(FFPC_LR, "k5"), 2)` and `r f(ffv(FFPC_LR, "k5", col = "hw_vs_reml"), 2)` times the
half-width. Two components (90% of the variance) truncate the surface: they cover the true $\beta$ at
`r f(ffv(FFPC_LR, "p090", col = "coverage"), 3)`, its projection onto the span of the estimated
components at `r f(ffv(FFPC_LR, "p090", col = "coverage_proj"), 3)`.

With the default covariate, whose spectrum decays slowly, the variance-explained rules choose many
components (median `r kr(ff_rich("p095", col = "K_median"))` for 95%,
`r kr(ff_rich("p090", col = "K_median"))` for 90%), and the estimates are noisy: relative RMSE
`r rng(ff_rich("p095"), 1)` at 95%, against `r rng(ff_rich("k3", "ff_reml_cl2"), 2)` for `ff()` with
REML. A fixed $K = 3$ has `r rng(ff_rich("k3") / ff_rich("k3", "ff_ncv_cl2"), 2)` times the relative
RMSE of `ff()` with NCV, but it truncates the surface, and its intervals undercover:
`r rng(ffv(ff_smooth_rich, "k3", col = "coverage"))` for smooth truths and
`r f(ffv(ff_rough, "k3", col = "coverage"), 2)` for the rough truth. With $K = 5$ they cover
`r rng(ff_rich("k5", col = "coverage"))` at `r rng(ff_rich("k5", col = "hw_vs_reml"), 2)` times the
half-width of `ff()` REML + CL2, with relative RMSE between those of `ff()` with NCV and with REML
in every setting. In a pilot with `r unique(ffp99$n_rep)` replicates of three of the settings, the
threshold of 0.99 (the default of current refund releases; at most 15 components) chose median $K$ of
`r kr(ffp99_v("ffpc_cl2", "K_median"))` and gave relative RMSE
`r rng(ffp99_v("ffpc_cl2"), 2)` (`ff()` with REML: `r rng(ffp99_v("ff_reml_cl2"), 2)`), also with
the low-rank covariate. The model-based intervals of the `ffpc()` fits cover
`r rng(FFPC$coverage[FFPC$arm == "ffpc_model"])` in all settings and rules.

These results are synthetic only. The smooth truth varies along $s$ mainly like the first cosine
functions, which are the covariate's leading principal components, so a small $K$ suits it. No rule
that chooses $K$ from the response, such as cross-validation, was evaluated, and there is no plasmode
check, in which truths fitted with `ff()` would not lie in the span of a few components.

```{r t-s1-ffpc}

ltab(
  ffpc_tab |> mutate(across(starts_with("K_"), as.character)),
  digits = c(0, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 3, 0, 2, 3, 0, 2, 3),
  col.names = c("setting", rep(c("rel.", "cov."), 4), rep(c("K", "rel.", "cov."), 2)),
  align = "lrrrrrrrrrrrrrr",
  caption = "Principal component term (ffpc) and ff, smooth errors, REML fits, 200 replicates: relative RMSE of $\\beta(s,t)$ pooled over replicates and grid (rel.) and grid-averaged coverage of nominal 95\\% CL2 intervals for the true $\\beta(s,t)$ (cov.); ff with REML + CL2 and NCV + CL2; ffpc with a fixed number $K$ of components or the number explaining 95\\% or 90\\% of the covariate's variance (K: median over replicates). Signal: default unless stated."
) |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "ff, REML" = 2, "ff, NCV" = 2, "ffpc, K = 3" = 2, "ffpc, K = 5" = 2, "ffpc, 95%" = 3, "ffpc, 90%" = 3)) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 7, latex_options = c("HOLD_position", "scale_down"))
```

# S2 Plasmode study {#sec-s3}

The datasets, the fitted models and the construction of the plasmode data are described in
Section 5.1 and Appendices B.2 and B.3 of the paper. In a replicate each subject's error is its fitted
residual curve with a random sign, so it takes only two values: the construction is a Rademacher wild
cluster bootstrap around the fitted residuals, which keeps each residual curve's shape and
within-curve covariance but not the full error distribution of new real curves. With curve flips (the
main design) the simulated errors are independent across curves for every dataset, including the three
whose source data have temporal or spatial dependence between curves (ocean, weather, electricity;
"datasets with dependent source curves" below); only the block flips of S2.3 share one sign within a
block of neighbouring curves. Coverage ranges are therefore also given over all nine datasets. All
plasmode truths are fits of the model itself, so the plasmode study cannot evaluate misspecification
of the mean, and the comparator results of S3 on plasmode data describe this generator, not real data
in general.

## S2.1 Coverage per dataset, truth source and residual source

```{r s3-3}
pm3 <- POOL_MEANS |> filter(arm %in% c("reml_model", "reml_cl2", "ncv_cl2"), estimand %in% c("mean", "beta"))
pmv3 <- \(a, e, r = "counted") pm3$coverage[pm3$arm == a & pm3$estimand == e & pm3$role == r]
g40v3 <- \(a, e = c("mean", "beta"), r = "counted") g40_app$loss[g40_app$arm == a & g40_app$estimand %in% e & g40_app$role == r]
aem <- P |>
  filter(app == "aemet", arm == "reml_cl2", estimand == "beta", flip == "curve", error == "attached", residual %in% c("REML", "NCV")) |>
  group_by(G_label) |>
  summarise(mn = mean(coverage_mean), lo = min(coverage_mean), hi = max(coverage_mean), G = max(G), .groups = "drop")
aem_g <- \(g, col) aem[[col]][aem$G_label == g]
aem_G <- aem$G[aem$G_label == "all"]
```

On the datasets with independent source curves (means over each dataset's truth × residual
combinations, all subjects), model-based intervals cover $\beta$ at `r rng(pmv3("reml_model", "beta"))` and the mean
at `r rng(pmv3("reml_model", "mean"))`; REML + CL2 covers them at `r rng(pmv3("reml_cl2", "beta"))` and
`r rng(pmv3("reml_cl2", "mean"))`; NCV + CL2 at `r rng(pmv3("ncv_cl2", "beta"))` and
`r rng(pmv3("ncv_cl2", "mean"))`. On the datasets with dependent source curves (curve flips, so
independent simulated errors) REML + CL2 covers $\beta$ at `r rng(pmv3("reml_cl2", "beta", "stress test"))`.
Over all nine datasets it covers $\beta$ at `r rng(pm3$coverage[pm3$arm == "reml_cl2" & pm3$estimand == "beta"])`.
The exception is weather: `r f(aem_g("all", "mn"))` on average (combinations `r rng(c(aem_g("all", "lo"), aem_g("all", "hi")))`)
with all `r aem_G` stations and `r f(aem_g("40", "mn"))` (`r rng(c(aem_g("40", "lo"), aem_g("40", "hi")))`) with 40,
on a covariate of rank `r as.integer(DATASETS$rank_X[DATASETS$app == "aemet"])`. With 40 subjects
REML + CL2 loses `r rng_pp(g40v3("reml_cl2"))` on the datasets with independent source curves. On the
datasets with independent source curves the ratio of REML + CL2's root mean square standard error to
the replicate SD of the estimate is `r rng(dpv("reml_cl2", "se_sd"))` (median over grid points;
S4.1(a)). For a centred normal estimator a ratio $r$ gives coverage of about $2\Phi(1.96\,r) - 1$,
for example `r f(2 * pnorm(1.96 * 0.9) - 1, 3)` at $r = 0.90$. The ratios are therefore consistent
with a standard error a little short and with residual bias; the shortfall was not decomposed further. Its lower tail for $\beta$
depends on the truth source: under the REML-fitted truth its 5% quantile on these datasets is
`r rng(cl2_truth[["q05 REML truth"]][cl2_truth$role == "counted"])`, under the NCV-fitted truth
`r rng(cl2_truth[["q05 NCV truth"]][cl2_truth$role == "counted"])`.

```{r f-s3-cov}
#| fig-height: 8.4
```

*Satterthwaite critical values.* With the per-point Satterthwaite critical value, REML + CL2 covers
$\beta$ at `r f(mean(spa("satt", "all")), 3)` on average over the nine datasets with all subjects and
`r f(mean(spa("satt", "40")), 3)` with 40 (normal critical value: `r f(mean(spa("z", "all")), 3)` and
`r f(mean(spa("z", "40")), 3)`), at `r f(mean(spa("satt", "all", col = "wr")), 2)` and
`r f(mean(spa("satt", "40", col = "wr")), 2)` times the width (next table; means over each dataset's
combinations of truth and residual source). Coverage stays below `r f(LEVEL - ADEQUATE, 2)` only for
`r sp_low_txt`. The curve flips make the simulated errors independent across curves, so these
shortfalls do not come from dependence between curves. The paired gain over the normal critical value
is positive in every combination (smallest `r pp(min(SATPC$diff[SATPC$contrast == "Satt - z"]), 2)`).

```{r t-s3-satt}
#| output: asis
stab(satp_tab |> rename(`E(Y|X) z` = `mean z`, `E(Y|X) Satt.` = `mean satt`, `β z` = `beta z`, `β Satt.` = `beta satt`, `α z` = `alpha z`, `α Satt.` = `alpha satt`, `γ z` = `gamma z`, `γ Satt.` = `gamma satt`, `width Satt./z` = width),
  "Plasmode study, curve flips: grid-averaged coverage of REML + CL2 with the normal ($z$) and the Satterthwaite (Satt.) critical value per dataset and number of subjects $G$ (mean over the dataset's combinations of truth and residual source), and the width ratio for $\\beta(s,t)$.", font = 6)
```

```{r t-s3-cov-1}
#| output: asis
p_arms <- c("REML, model-based" = "REML model", "REML + CL2" = "REML+CL2", "NCV + CL2" = "NCV+CL2",
  "NCV + CL2, widened by NCV–REML difference" = "NCV wid.", "AR(1) working model" = "AR(1)")
p_est <- c("β(s,t)", "E(Y | X)")
p_w <- supp_p_wide |>
  mutate(dataset = as.character(dataset), truth = dplyr::coalesce(unname(truth_lab[truth]), truth)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = estimand, values_from = all_of(names(p_arms)), names_glue = "{estimand}|{.value}")
p_cols <- paste0(rep(p_est, each = length(p_arms)), "|", names(p_arms))
p_w <- relabel(p_w[, c(setdiff(names(p_w), p_cols), p_cols)])
p_id <- ncol(p_w) - length(p_cols)
k <- knitr::kable(p_w, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, longtable = TRUE, linesep = "",
  col.names = c(names(p_w)[seq_len(p_id)], rep(unname(p_arms), 2)),
  caption = "Grid-averaged coverage (MC SE) per plasmode combination and interval, for $\\beta(s,t)$ and the mean. REML model: model-based REML interval; NCV wid.: NCV + CL2 widened by the NCV–REML difference; AR(1): AR(1) working model.")
k <- kableExtra::kable_styling(k, font_size = 5, latex_options = "repeat_header") |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(c(setNames(p_id, " "), setNames(rep(length(p_arms), 2), p_est))) |>
  kableExtra::landscape()
cat("\\begingroup\\renewcommand{\\arraystretch}{0.9}\n", k, "\n\\endgroup\n", sep = "")
```

The NCV/REML MSE ratio for $\beta$ (geometric mean over residual sources, all subjects) is
`r rng(rt("NCV", "beta"))` under the NCV-fitted truth, `r rng(rt("MID", "beta"))` under the

(`r paste(APP_LABELS[losers3$app], collapse = ", ")`). A truth taken from one fit has that fit's

(next table): $\beta$ is weakly determined by these covariates.

# S3 Comparators {#sec-s4}

## S3.1 AR(1) working model

The AR(1) working model fits the REML model with an AR(1) residual correlation along $t$, $\rho$
profiled (mgcv `bam`), and uses its model-based intervals. On stationary homoskedastic synthetic
errors it covers `r rng(av("ar1_model", c("ou", "fpc", "ou0", "osc")))` (Gaussian, $G = 100$; next
table). It fails under misregistration (mean
`r rng(ar1_tab$ar1_model[ar1_tab$error == "warp" & ar1_tab$estimand == "mean"])`, $\beta$
`r rng(ar1_tab$ar1_model[ar1_tab$error == "warp" & ar1_tab$estimand == "beta"])`), for $\gamma(t)$
under covariate-dependent variance, and in the plasmode study: with the midpoint truth and REML
residuals it covers the mean at `r rng(ar1_v("mean"))` and $\beta$ at `r rng(ar1_v("beta"))` across the
nine datasets. Median fit time: `r f(median(TIMING$fit_time[TIMING$method == "AR1"]), 0)` s against
`r f(median(TIMING$fit_time[TIMING$method == "REML"]), 1)` s for REML (Appendix C of the paper).

```{r t-s4-ar1}
  "AR(1) working model (Gaussian, $G = 100$): coverage next to REML intervals, interval score relative to REML + CL2, MSE relative to NCV (95% bootstrap interval).", font = 6)
```
